risorseHub.metaDesc: Free tools and resources from GeoTapp: the guide to GPS worker monitoring across Europe, the ROI calculator and the proof-of-work survey.
risorseHub.intro:
Free tools, guides and data to make field work provable.
We keep them updated and add new ones.

gps.title: GPS monitoring of workers in the EU

gpsPresenze.title: GPS for attendance, without tracking

autovalutazione.title: Are you data-compliant?
autovalutazione.desc: Quick 9-question test on protecting employee data: score and areas to fix. Free, in your browser.

generatore.title: GPS notice generator
generatore.desc: Create your customised GPS privacy notice with your logo, built to reflect GDPR requirements. Free, in your browser.

conservazione.title: Data retention policy
conservazione.desc: Generate the personnel data retention table by country: recommended periods, legal note and export. Free, in your browser.

sanzioni.title: GPS penalty calculator
sanzioni.desc: Pick a country and find out how much you risk monitoring workers: the highest fine actually imposed, or the legal maximum, and the obligations that expose you.

osservatorio.title: European observatory
osservatorio.desc: Decisions from Europe's data protection authorities on location tracking, CCTV and time recording at work, each one linked to its official source.

indice.title: Worker surveillance index in Europe
indice.desc: What the decisions published by European authorities say, in numbers, about monitoring workers: how many, on which topics, the biggest fines.

roi.title: ROI calculator
roi.desc: Estimate how much time and money you get back by using GeoTapp on your field operations.

survey.title: Survey: proof of work
survey.desc: Two minutes, anonymous: do you trust someone's word, or do you need proof? Help us understand a real problem.

items.q: Are the resources free?
items.a: Yes, all of them. The maps, the calculators, the privacy-notice generator and the country dossiers are free to use. They're how we share what we've studied about monitoring workers, even if you never become a customer.

items.q: Do I have to sign up or leave my email to use them?
items.a: No. You open the tool and use it. The privacy-notice generator runs inside your browser and sends your data nowhere; the other tools don't ask for an account. If you want to stay updated you can leave us your email, but that's your call, not a toll.

items.q: Can I trust the legal information here?
items.a: It's built on national law and real decisions by the authorities, with the source given and a verification date. That said, it stays an informative resource, not legal advice: before switching a monitoring system on, have your situation checked by a professional.

items.q: Can I use these tools on my own site?
items.a: Yes. The GPS workers map can be embedded with the code on its page, and the resources can be cited by linking the source. If you run an industry blog or advise companies, they're meant for that too.

items.q: Are they only useful if I use GeoTapp?
items.a: No, they stand on their own. We built them so that anyone sending people into the field understands what compliance takes, whether you use GeoTapp or not. If you then want a system that records location only at clock-in and never continuously, GeoTapp is built that way; the resources are useful either way.

items.q: Who are they for?
items.a: For anyone with teams working off-site: cleaning firms, installers, security, maintenance, construction. Anyone who has to prove where and when a job was done, and wants to do it without turning employees into dots on a map all day.

nexus-core.name: Job Management
nexus-core.short: Create and manage technical interventions. Assign tasks to technicians, monitor progress and keep everything tracked per job.
nexus-core.full:
### Every Job in One Place.

Every intervention starts as a structured job.
**Job Management** gives you a clear view of all work in progress.

#### Intervention Management

Create a job, assign the technician, define the site and date.
Follow the status: Open, In Progress, Completed.

#### Operational History

Every job has a complete archive of activities, photo proofs, notes and clock-ins.
The client asks what was done? You have the data.

titan-flow.name: Task Assignment
titan-flow.short: Distribute work to technicians with precision. Communicate instructions, deadlines and operational priorities in a structured way.
titan-flow.full:
### The Right Job to the Right Technician.

Confused task assignment generates delays and disputes.
**Task Assignment** brings operational clarity.

#### Precise Distribution

As soon as a job is opened, assign one or more technicians.
Each technician sees their work on GeoTapp TimeTracker.

#### Operational Communication

Instructions, notes, technical attachments: everything reaches the technician before they leave for the field.
Fewer calls, fewer misunderstandings, fewer delays.

ledger-prime.name: Reports and Billing
ledger-prime.short: Generate structured reports from every job. Export documentation and support billing with real field data.
ledger-prime.full:
### From Work to Report, in an Orderly Way.

Manual billing is slow and often incomplete.
**Reports and Billing** closes the operational cycle.

#### Structured Reports

Every completed intervention generates documentation by collecting timestamps, photos and notes from the field.
No data to enter manually, it all comes from TimeTracker.

#### Billing Support

Real job data supports more accurate quotes and invoices.
Fewer errors, fewer disputes, faster administrative cycle.

quantum-logistics.name: Intervention Calendar
quantum-logistics.short: Plan interventions, visualise the operational calendar and manage team availability without overlaps.
quantum-logistics.full:
### Full View of Planned Work.

Without a shared calendar, planning becomes chaotic.
**Intervention Calendar** gives you clear operational visibility.

#### Advanced Planning

View all interventions on daily, weekly and monthly calendar views.
Identify overlaps and optimise workload distribution.

#### Team Availability

See who is available, who is on leave and who is already overloaded.
Assign new interventions without creating operational conflicts.

supply-command.name: Resource Management
supply-command.short: Keep the catalogue, suppliers and materials linked to your jobs, so the technician leaves with what is needed.
supply-command.full:
### No Intervention Short of Resources.

Sending a technician to the field without the right materials is a costly mistake.
**Resource Management** prevents operational surprises.

#### Catalogue and Jobs

Keep your product catalogue in Flow and link it to quotes and jobs.
The manager sees in advance what is needed and when.

#### Suppliers

Store contact details and terms for your regular suppliers.
Reduce procurement time and keep costs under control.

the-architect.name: Work Planning
the-architect.short: Organise work into phases, tasks and deadlines. Keep the project under control without spreadsheets or WhatsApp messages.
the-architect.full:
### Structure the Work. Control the Progress.

Complex jobs require structure.
**Work Planning** brings operational order.

#### Phases and Deadlines

Structure complex interventions into operational phases with clear deadlines.
Assign responsibilities to each team member.

#### Progress Monitoring

Follow progress, updated step by step.
Always know what has been done and what remains open.
Act before a delay becomes a client problem.

the-auditor.name: Intervention Documentation
the-auditor.short: Collect photo evidence, operational notes and documents for every intervention. Work performed stays verifiable.
the-auditor.full:
### Real Proof for Every Intervention.

Without documentation, completed work is contestable.
**Intervention Documentation** makes every job verifiable.

#### Photo Evidence

Technicians take photos directly from GeoTapp TimeTracker on the field.
Images are automatically linked to the job with time and location.

#### Sealed Report

At the end of the job the system generates a digitally sealed report: any later change stays detectable.
The client can check it alone, without needing to log in to GeoTapp.

the-uplink.name: Field-to-Office Link
the-uplink.short: Data collected by TimeTracker arrives in Flow as soon as it is recorded. Field and office work on the same operational data.
the-uplink.full:
### Office and Field, Finally Connected.

The distance between field and office generates avoidable errors, delays and disputes.
**Field-to-Office Link** shortens it.

#### Immediate Arrival

Every clock-in, photo and note recorded on TimeTracker arrives in Flow as soon as it is sent.
The manager sees the data without having to call the technician.

#### Reliable History

Everything the technician records on the field stays archived and linked to the job.
When it is time to report, the data is already there.

the-oracle.name: Operational Visibility
the-oracle.short: Operational dashboard updated with every intervention. Always know how many interventions are open, in progress or completed today.
the-oracle.full:
### Operational Data, Not Assumptions.

Deciding without reliable data is dangerous.
**Operational Visibility** turns field data into concrete information.

#### Operational Dashboard

See, updated with every intervention:
- Open and in-progress interventions
- Active technicians
- Interventions completed today and this week

#### Periodic Reports

Receive automated activity summaries.
Compare periods, identify bottlenecks and optimise operations.

app.hero_title:

app.hero_subtitle: The app technicians use to clock in, take proof photos and stay connected to the office directly from the field. Available on Android and iOS.
app.grid_subtitle: Every feature is designed for those who work outside the office and have no time to waste. Click to learn more.

timelock-alpha.name: GPS Time Tracking
timelock-alpha.short: Start, breaks and finish record location and the exact time at the moment of clocking in. Every shift becomes data the client can verify.
timelock-alpha.full:
### The Right Time, in the Right Place.

Clock-ins without a check generate disputes.
**GPS Time Tracking** makes every shift reliable data.

#### Start, Breaks and Finish

The technician clocks in from the phone.
Location, address and time are recorded at that moment, and only then: nothing is automatically recorded between one clock-in and the next.

#### Sealed History

Every shift is a record: start time, end time, breaks, position, duration and job.
In the report handed to the client it is sealed: any later change is detectable.

event-horizon.name: Shift Planning
event-horizon.short: Manage shifts and staff availability. Weekly and monthly views for coordination without confusion or overlaps.
event-horizon.full:
### No Shift Conflicts.

Organising mobile personnel requires clarity.
**Shift Planning** gives the manager a precise, up-to-date view.

#### Calendar View

See who works when.
Identify absences, holidays and overlaps before they become operational problems.

#### Always Up-to-date Availability

Employees confirm attendance or report absences directly from the app.
The manager sees gaps in the schedule before assigning new jobs.

unit-matrix.name: Operator Registry
unit-matrix.short: Keep your operators in order: roles, contacts and platform access, with new people up and running in minutes.
unit-matrix.full:
### Know Your Team.

Every operator is a key operational resource.
**Operator Registry** keeps together the information you need.

#### Roles and Access

Decide who sees what: administrator, manager, operator.
Each person accesses only what their role allows.

#### Quick Onboarding

Adding a new technician is simple.
Send an invite code: they sign the GPS notice and within minutes they are clocking in on GeoTapp TimeTracker.

sector-grid.name: Sites and Worksites
sector-grid.short: Create a database of operational sites and worksites. Link each intervention to the correct location and organise teams by zone.
sector-grid.full:
### Every Intervention in the Right Place.

Working without geographic reference generates confusion.
**Sites and Worksites** brings operational clarity.

#### Site Database

Create a catalogue of client sites, worksites and operational locations.
The system automatically links technician activity to the intervention site.

#### Zone-based Teams

Organise technicians into teams by site or geographic area.
Assign interventions to the correct team, not just the individual.

energy-logistics.name: Vehicle and Expense Management
energy-logistics.short: Record company car use during the shift, refuelling and travel expenses, with a photo of the receipt.
energy-logistics.full:
### Every Expense Documented.

Travel expenses are a delicate item for any company with staff on the move.
**Vehicle and Expense Management** puts them in order.

#### Vehicle Use

Assign a vehicle to an employee for an intervention, and the operator declares in the app whether they use the car during the shift.
You know who used which vehicle and for which job.

#### Fuel Expenses

The employee records refuelling from the app, with a receipt photo and amount.
The office approves the reimbursement, and everything stays linked to the job.

neural-link.name: Operational Communications
neural-link.short: Internal channel for company communications. Targeted messages to specific groups with read confirmations.
neural-link.full:
### Clear Communications. No Background Noise.

WhatsApp mixes private and professional life and offers no control over read status.
**Operational Communications** is the official company channel.

#### Targeted Messages

Notify only the team that needs to know.
Shift change at the Rome site? Only the assigned technicians receive the message.

#### Read Confirmations

Always know who read the communication and who did not.
Clear and transparent accountability for everyone.

payroll-bridge.name: Attendance Export
payroll-bridge.short: Export the month's attendance to Excel or CSV, ready for your payroll consultant. Less manual work, fewer errors.
payroll-bridge.full:
### Payroll Without Headaches.

Month end does not have to be an administrative nightmare.
**Attendance Export** connects field work to personnel administration.

#### Excel and CSV

Hours, overtime, surcharges and absences come out in an Excel or CSV file ready to hand to your payroll consultant.

#### Consultant Access

Give your payroll firm a separate access, the Accountant portal.
They download the data they need independently, without calling you every month end.

data-core.name: Weekly Reports
data-core.short: Detailed reports on hours worked per job and per operator. Reliable data for internal control and billing.
data-core.full:
### Decide on Facts.

Make decisions based on data, not impressions.
**Weekly Reports** lines up each day's work.

#### Detailed Reports

Every week, a complete picture: who worked, where, on which job and for how many hours.

#### The Same Numbers for Everyone

Employees and managers look at the same report.
Hours counted are identical for everyone, and there is much less to argue about at month end.

identity-forge.name: Branded App
identity-forge.short: Upload your logo and choose your company colours. Your operators use an app that reflects your brand identity.
identity-forge.full:
### Your Company, Your App.

Do not use a generic app.
Make your employees feel part of YOUR company with a consistent visual experience.

#### Company Logo

Your logo prominently displayed on the login screen and main dashboard.

#### Company Colours

Choose the colour theme that fits your corporate image.
Professional, consistent, recognisable.

chi_siamo.hero_desc: The product started from a sheet of paper with a month of hours on it, and totals that never added up.
story: There is one job nobody has ever been paid to do, and it is writing down the hours you worked. Date, start, end, total. Every day, and at the end of the month the tally goes to the boss.

Michele Angelo Petraroli worked event security, as an employee, and he filled in that sheet the way everybody fills it in, which is badly. The totals almost never matched, partly his own fault, because it is human to put off the boring things and rebuild them from memory a week later.

He went looking for an app to take the chore away. They were all the same, and every one of them asked for exactly what he was already doing by hand: date, start, end, total. Same effort, nicer buttons.
So he built one himself, on holiday. A web page and two gestures: press when you start and press when you stop, and the rest landed tidy in a file already fit to send at the end of the month.

Then came the thought that changed everything: if it helps me, it helps the crew. And if it helps the boss, the flow has to be turned around, because it should not be him chasing people for their hours: it should be the hours reaching him every day, on their own.

From there the tool grew in one direction only. First geolocation designed to stay within the law: the position is read only when the worker clocks in (start, breaks, finish) and never continuously. Then verifiable proof of the work done, because the real problem was never counting the hours, it was proving them when somebody questioned them.
Oh, and it is spelled GeoTapp, with two P's. If you find one with a single P out there, that is not us, though we hold no grudge.
The name has it all in it, really: geolocation, a tap, an app.

founder.name: Michele Angelo Petraroli
founder.bio: Michele Angelo Petraroli is the founder and owner of GeoTapp, the Italian software that documents the work of field crews in European SMEs. From direct experience in service SMEs (cleaning, installers, security) he saw how much money is lost when there is no proof of the work done. He founded GeoTapp in 2024 to solve the problem at the source. Today GeoTapp helps European SMEs prove the work they have done: location recorded only when someone clocks in, proof photos and sealed reports the client can verify alone.

stampa.boilerplate_short: GeoTapp is a time-tracking and proof-of-work tool for companies with field teams. It records where and when a clock-in happens only at the moment the worker clocks in, never continuously, and produces a document the client can verify independently.
stampa.boilerplate_long: GeoTapp started from a concrete problem: proving that a job was done, where and when, without turning people into dots on a map to be watched all day. The tool records location only at the moment the worker clocks in, takes a break or clocks out, and nothing automatically in between; it adds proof photos and notes from the field, and seals every session so that any change is detectable. The result is proof the client can verify independently, one that protects the employer facing a dispute as much as the worker wrongly accused of not showing up. It is built for anyone sending teams off-site, cleaning firms, installers, security, maintenance, construction, and designed to stay within the limits of worker-monitoring law and the GDPR.

faq.q: How is the ROI of a GPS time-tracking app calculated?
faq.a: The estimate is built from three concrete items: the admin hours saved every month, the disputes and unwarranted overtime that proof of work helps avoid, and the coordination time recovered. The yearly total is compared with the subscription cost to produce ROI and payback time.

faq.q: Do I need to register or leave an email to see the result?
faq.a: No. The calculation is instant and free: enter your figures and see the estimate straight away. Email is optional and only used if you want the detailed breakdown and practical guides.

faq.q: What data is the estimated saving based on?
faq.a: Only the values you enter: number of operators, sites or job sites managed, hours spent on admin, hourly cost and the disputes typical of your sector. The more realistic your inputs, the closer the estimate is to your situation.

faq.q: Does the estimated saving already include the cost of the subscription?
faq.a: The total you see is the gross saving. The payback time and the ROI percentage, on the other hand, compare it against the annual cost of the tool, worked out on the number of operators you entered. So the percentage is already net, the total is not.

faq.q: What does the payback time in months actually mean?
faq.a: It is how many months of estimated saving it takes to cover one year of the tool. Anything under twelve means the tool pays for itself inside the first year, and what comes after that is margin you get back.

faq.q: Why does the calculation not recover all the admin hours?
faq.a: Because it stays deliberately cautious: it counts about two thirds of those hours, not all of them. Some paperwork stays no matter what, and an estimate promising a hundred per cent would be a sales figure, not a forecast.

features.gps_title: Location only when you clock in
features.gps_desc: Location is recorded when the worker clocks in (start, breaks, finish) and when they take a proof photo. Nothing is automatically recorded between one clock-in and the next. In Flow, the Today's clock-ins screen shows each clock-in with its location and the check against the place of work: the office knows who started where without calling anyone, and the team knows exactly what is recorded, and when.
features.offline_title: One-tap clock-in, even without a signal
features.offline_desc: One tap to start the shift, mark breaks and close it. Every job can have its proof photos. If there is no signal, the clock-in stays saved on the phone and is sent on its own when the signal returns, with the time at which it was made.
features.encryption_desc: At clock-in the app rejects locations simulated by fake-location apps, ones that are too imprecise and impossible jumps. On photos nothing is rejected: they are flagged, by comparing the time and location of the shot with those of the clock-in.
features.realtime_desc: At the end of the job the report is built from clock-ins, photos and notes, and sealed: a chain of SHA-256 fingerprints links every event and every photo, and the root is signed with GeoTapp's key. Any later change is detectable.
features.cms_desc: The client receives a link and checks the report alone, online or with the offline verifier: a single file that does not connect to the internet and carries the public key inside. It works even years from now, even without GeoTapp.
features.datalake_title: Data in Europe, kept for the right time
features.datalake_desc: The service data sits on servers in the European Union and travels encrypted. In the register, locations are deleted after twelve months, a period the company can shorten down to thirty days; in reports already delivered they remain, because they are sealed documents, and after five years the package is deleted.

risorseGps.metaTitleSelettore: GPS and worker monitoring in Europe: what you need to stay compliant, country by country
risorseGps.metaDescSelettore: Choose a country and find out what it takes to make GPS and worker monitoring compliant: obligations, procedure, authority and a template to download.
risorseGps.h1Selettore: GPS and worker monitoring, country by country
risorseGps.introSelettore: Same Europe, different rules. You send a crew to install, clean or guard in another country and assume the rules on GPS and worker monitoring are the ones from home. They are not. Every state has its own, and they apply where the work happens: a company with a site abroad follows the local rules, even if the crew is only there on a posting. Choose the destination and we tell you what it takes to be compliant: the obligations, the procedure, who to contact and the template to download.

risorseGps.cosaServeLegenda: For each obligation we tell you whether it applies in this country: Yes means required, It depends means only in certain cases, No means not required.
risorseGps.disclaimer: This is an informational resource, not legal advice. Before activating a monitoring system, have your situation checked by a professional.
risorseGps.ctaTitolo: Want a system built to stay within the rules?
risorseGps.ctaTesto: GeoTapp records the location only when someone clocks in or takes a proof photo, never continuously, and has the notice signed in the app before the first clock-in. Try it for free.

items.q: Can I use GPS to keep an eye on my crew while they work?
items.a: GPS at work is legal almost everywhere in Europe, on one condition: it has to organise and prove the work, not watch the person. The how is what counts. Recording location at clock-in, when someone starts, takes a break and finishes, is a very different thing from following them in real time all day. The first can almost always be done properly, the second almost never. What "properly" means changes from country to country, though, and it is not only about documents: sometimes an agreement with the workers' representatives or a specific legal basis is needed. The page for your country, above, says what it really takes.

items.q: Do my own country's rules apply, or the country where I send the team?
items.a: The country where the work happens. If your company is based in Ireland but the job site is in France, you follow the French rules, even if the crew is there for a two-week stint. That's why this page asks you to pick the destination first: the obligations shift from one state to the next, and what's enough at home can fall short across the border.

items.q: Do I need the worker's consent?
items.a: Consent is rarely the right route, which catches a lot of people out. In an employment relationship consent is treated as not freely given, because the person who refuses fears the fallout, so regulators prefer other grounds: the company's legitimate interest or a contractual duty, paired with a clear privacy notice. In several countries you also need a step with the union or a workplace agreement before you switch anything on.

items.q: Can I track location in real time, all day long?
items.a: That's the exact thing that triggers the fines. Continuous tracking is considered disproportionate almost everywhere: you record far more than you need to pay the hours or prove a job. The practical rule is to collect the minimum, the location at the moment that matters, not a thread that trails the person from morning to night.

items.q: What's the risk if I switch a system on without being compliant?
items.a: It depends on the country, but GDPR fines climb to numbers no small business wants to see, and in some states there are labour-law consequences on top. The real problem, though, often isn't the fine: it's that data collected the wrong way becomes useless exactly when you need it, in a dispute or in front of a client who's contesting the bill. Each country sheet shows the legal maximum and, where one exists, the fine actually issued in a real case.

items.q: Is GeoTapp a surveillance system?
items.a: No, it is not designed to watch people. It records location at every clock-in (start, break, finish) and when a proof photo is taken; between one clock-in and the next it records nothing automatically. And it produces the privacy notice for workers to sign. It is there to prove what was done and where, not to watch people. That is the difference between proof of work and a leash.

regoleComuni.titolo: The rules that apply across the whole of Europe
regoleComuni.intro: Before looking at a single country it helps to know what never changes. The GDPR applies identically in every member state, and these six principles hold everywhere. National employment law sits on top, and that is the part that changes at every border.

regole.titolo: A legitimate purpose, declared up front
regole.testo: Organising work, protecting safety, documenting the job. Never 'checking up on the person': that is not an admissible purpose (Articles 5 and 6 GDPR).

regole.titolo: Only the data you need, only when you need it
regole.testo: This is data minimisation (Article 5(1)(c)). Recording position at the start and end of a job documents it; recording every minute monitors the person.
Workers must know in advance what is recorded, when, why and for how long (Articles 12 and 13). A generic notice, or one that does not match the real system, counts as no notice at all.
Data is kept for the period necessary for the purpose, decided and written down in advance, not 'for as long as it is useful' (Article 5(1)(e)).

regole.titolo: An impact assessment where the risk is high
regole.testo: Systematic monitoring of workers typically falls among the cases requiring a DPIA (Article 35), to be carried out before the system is switched on, not afterwards.

regole.titolo: Data collected for one purpose is not reused for another
regole.testo: This is purpose limitation (Article 5(1)(b)). Positions collected to document work do not automatically become evidence in a disciplinary case.

regoleComuni.nota: Then there is Article 88 GDPR, which lets each state add its own rules on data processing in the employment relationship. That is why the country cards below exist: what changes is who has to authorise you, not the principle.

items.q: What's the real risk if GPS isn't compliant?
items.a: It depends on the country and on what went wrong, but GDPR fines aren't symbolic: they can reach a percentage of turnover, and in several states there are labour-law consequences on top. Pick the country above and you will see the highest figure, and whether it is a fine actually issued or the legal maximum.

items.q: Do GDPR fines really hit small businesses?
items.a: Yes, and the idea that regulators only go after the big players is one of the beliefs that costs the most. The cases listed on each country sheet include outfits of a handful of people, fined precisely for monitoring staff without the paperwork in order. Size affects the amount, not whether you're in the firing line.

items.q: Is the fine the only risk?
items.a: No, and it's often not even the worst one. Data collected the wrong way becomes useless exactly when you need it, in a dispute with an employee or in front of a client contesting an invoice. You end up with the fine to pay and without the proof you thought you had.

items.q: Can I be fined even if the workers agreed?
items.a: Yes, because in an employment relationship consent counts for little: the person who gives it is assumed not to be truly free to refuse. Regulators look at whether the processing was proportionate and whether you had solid grounds and a clear privacy notice, not at whether someone signed a sheet. The workers' agreement on its own doesn't protect you.

items.q: Where do these figures come from?
items.a: From real decisions by data protection authorities and from national law, not from estimates. Each sheet gives the source and the case, so you can trace it back to the document. This is an informative resource, not legal advice: before switching a system on, have your situation checked by a professional.

items.q: How do I lower the risk of a fine?
items.a: By collecting the bare minimum you actually need: location at clock-in, not continuous tracking, with a signed privacy notice and a basis other than consent. That is exactly how GeoTapp was developed, and the privacy-notice generator here in the resources prepares the document for them to sign.

indiceSorveglianza.metaTitle: Worker surveillance index in Europe: the 39-country ranking
indiceSorveglianza.metaDesc: Which European countries have the strictest rules on worker monitoring? Ranking by severity index, with maximum fine and source. 39 countries.
indiceSorveglianza.intro: Europe doesn't treat worker surveillance the same way everywhere. We ranked 39 countries by how strict the framework is: more required obligations, higher the index. Click the columns to re-sort.
indiceSorveglianza.metodologia: The index (0-100) measures how many worker-monitoring obligations are mandatory in that country: score = required obligations + half of the conditional ones, over the total. Higher = stricter framework for anyone wanting to track. Data derived from the source-verified country pages; it ranks compliance burden, not 'freedom'.

items.q: What does the workplace surveillance index measure?
items.a: How strict each country's framework is on monitoring workers: the number of mandatory obligations, the steps required before switching a system on, and the weight of the penalties. The higher the score, the more you have to put in order before using GPS or any staff monitoring in that country.

items.q: Does a high score mean GPS is banned there?
items.a: No, it means more care is needed, not that it's forbidden. Almost everywhere in Europe GPS at work is allowed, as long as it's used to organise and prove the work and not to watch the person. A high index just tells you the obligations are heavier and that improvising gets expensive.

items.q: Where does the ranking data come from?
items.a: From the 39 country dossiers on the site, built on national law and real decisions by the authorities. The ranking distils them into a comparable score; click a country and you reach the sheet with the obligations, the competent authority and the sources.

items.q: Why do neighbouring countries score so differently?
items.a: Because GDPR sets the frame but each state adds its own rules on top, and on monitoring workers the differences are sharp: where a union agreement is needed, where a privacy notice is enough, where the authority is more aggressive. That's why taking your home rules for granted across the border is the mistake that triggers the fines.

items.q: How often is it updated?
items.a: The sheets carry the verification date and are reviewed when the law changes or new decisions come out. This is an informative resource, not legal advice: before switching a system on, have your situation checked by a professional.

items.q: How do I use the ranking if I send teams abroad?
items.a: Start from the country where they'll be working, not yours: the rules there are the ones that apply. Look at the score to gauge how much work is ahead, then open the sheet for the exact obligations and prepare the privacy notice to be signed before the trip.

accessibilita.title: Accessibility statement
accessibilita.intro: GeoTapp is committed to making this website accessible, in line with Directive (EU) 2019/882 (European Accessibility Act) and the EN 301 549 standard, which refers to the WCAG 2.1 level AA guidelines.
accessibilita.stato: This website is **partially conformant** with EN 301 549 / WCAG 2.1 AA. «Partially» means that some requirements are met and verified, while others have not yet been tested with full automated and manual methods.
accessibilita.fatto: An automated analysis with axe-core, run in a real browser on 23 September 2026, across twenty-two pages in the eleven published languages. The issues found were fixed: text contrast, accessible names for form fields, link names, correct use of ARIA attributes. The site declares the language of each page, offers a «skip to content» link, uses semantic landmarks, shows a visible keyboard focus, and honours the system preference for reduced motion.
accessibilita.limiti: A full manual review with screen readers and keyboard-only navigation has not yet been carried out. The purchase flow is hosted on a separate domain (crm.geotapp.com) and is not covered by this statement. Blog content and downloadable PDF documents have not been checked individually.
accessibilita.metodo: Self-assessment carried out internally, using automated tools on published pages. No third-party audit has been performed.
accessibilita.segnala: If you encounter a barrier on this site, write to info@geotapp.com stating the page and what you were unable to do. We reply within thirty days. If the reply is not satisfactory, you may contact the competent enforcement authority in your country.
accessibilita.data: Statement written on 23 September 2026, based on the assessment of the same date.
